children: Thermal coal prices are softening amid rising hopes for easing the Middle East conflict, says Commonwealth Bank of Australia's John Oh. President Trump has signaled that further U.S. military strikes on Iran aren't necessary for now. The conflict has spurred gains in coal prices this year. "With 20% of pre‑war LNG supply disrupted by the U.S.‑Iran conflict, the rise of thermal coal prices has been driven by gas‑to‑coal switching in the power sector," says Oh. Australian Newcastle futures are down 5.6% from a week ago and 7.6% lower month-on-month. Richards Bay thermal-coal prices have also eased. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
